reviewed_by: Claude Sonnet blind reviewer, batch B2 (g1 na_q2-q4 + g2 dp/mg), 2026-08-12

samples_reviewed.question_text: Make a picture graph to show: cats: 10, dogs: 10, birds: 10, fish: 10. Each 🍎 equals 10.
Make a picture graph to show: apples: 10, bananas: 6, mangoes: 16, grapes: 12. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Make a picture graph to show: roses: 15, sunflowers: 15, tulips: 15, daisies: 5. Each 🍎 equals 5.
Make a picture graph to show: Monday: 10, Tuesday: 10, Wednesday: 10, Thursday: 5. Each 🍎 equals 5.
Make a picture graph to show: cats: 14, dogs: 2, birds: 8, fish: 18. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Make a picture graph to show: Grade 1: 45, Grade 2: 40, Grade 3: 25, Grade 4: 35, Grade 5: 20, Grade 6: 10. Each 🍎 equals 5.
Make a picture graph to show: Monday: 30, Tuesday: 20, Wednesday: 30, Thursday: 30, Friday: 30, Saturday: 20. Each 🍎 equals 10.
Make a picture graph to show: basketball: 20, volleyball: 30, swimming: 20, running: 40, soccer: 10, tennis: 40. Each 🍎 equals 10.
Make a picture graph to show: Monday: 13, Tuesday: 16, Wednesday: 6, Thursday: 5. Draw one 🍎 for each item.
Make a picture graph to show: Math: 10, Science: 10, English: 10, Art: 10. Each 🍎 equals 10.
Make a picture graph to show: roses: 6, sunflowers: 12, tulips: 18, daisies: 10. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Make a picture graph to show: red: 15, blue: 15, green: 10, yellow: 10. Each 🍎 equals 5.
Make a picture graph to show: cats: 8, dogs: 14, birds: 12, fish: 12. Each 🍎 equals 2.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every stem asks the student to build a picture graph from raw category counts, 'Make a picture graph to show: cats: 10, dogs: 10, birds: 10, fish: 10. Each 🍎 equals 10.', matching the 'in a pictograph with a scale' half of the competency.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All thirteen sampled items go the same single direction, raw data into a pictograph; none tests the 'vice versa' direction the competency text explicitly names, where a pictograph would need to be read back into tabular or raw form.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Category counts stay small (4 to 6 categories, values up to 45) and the scale is stated plainly, matching what a Grade 2 Quarter 3 learner is expected to plot.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Scale factors of 2, 5, and 10 all occur, and one item drops to a 1-to-1 scale ('Draw one 🍎 for each item'), giving several distinct construction sub-tasks even though the overall direction never varies.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty rises through the number of categories and the size of the scale factor rather than shifting to an unrelated skill, keeping every item about pictograph construction.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Scale factors of 2, 5, and 10 and category totals up to 45 fit comfortably within what Grade 2 data work expects, without inflating past reasonable classroom counts.
